To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

El Nino winters are associated with an enhanced probability of stratospheric sudden warming events in the polar stratosphere, and the enhanced probability is associated with the tropical SST anomalies that induce changes of the wave 1 and wave 2 in high latitudes, which in turn affect the wave forcing entering the lower stratospheric polar vortex.

El Nino winters have twice the occurrence of stratospheric sudden warming (SSW) as La Nina winters, and this is due to changes in the PDFs of the wave forcing entering the winter stratosphere, which are induced by tropical SST anomalies that mimic the observed El Nino and the La Nina conditions.

1) El Nino winters have a higher occurrence frequency of SSWs than La Nina winters; 2) the enhanced occurrence of SSWs is caused by a shift of the shape of PDFs of stratospheric variability; 3) the tropical SST anomalies that cause the shift are associated with the enhancement of wave 1 in the upper tropo- and stratosphere, which is a result of a tropical wave response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the mechanisms of the observed El Nino effect on SSW occurrence.
the role of the troposphere in modulating SSW occurrence.
the role of the tropical Pacific in the stratosphere and how this role is manifested in the observed stratospheric sudden warming (SSW) statistics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the El Nino conditions are conducive to more frequent and stronger SSWs in winter.
El Nino conditions are associated with a warmer polar vortex and a weaker stratospheric polar night jet in the Northern Hemisphere, which is in basic agreement with observational evidence.
the El Nino conditions lead to more SSWs by enhancing the planetary wave 1 in the upper tropopause and the lower stratospheric polar vortex, and by shifting the PDF of the stratospheric wave forcing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that El Nino leads to more SSWs by enhancing the wave forcing entering the polar lower stratosphere through a combination of changes to the wave 1 and wave 2.
we show that the increased frequency of SSW during El Nino is due to the enhanced planetary wave 1, which is a result of the tropical SST forcing.

the increased frequency of SSWs in El Nino is a consequence of the enhanced planetary wave activity in the upper tropospheric and stratosphere, which is induced by El Nino in the tropics and propagates to high latitudes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased occurrence of SSWs in El Nino years is due to the increased occurrence of strong wave events.
El Nino conditions in the tropics lead to a stronger stratosphere and more stratospheric sudden warming.
the El Nino-SST forcing induces an increase in the frequency of SSWs, and that the increase is due to an enhancement of the wave forcing entering the lower stratospheric vortex.
